Q: Trying to create a function(python) that looks at a list of strings, takes input, then based on the input, either(appends, pops, quits, removes items) A:

I'm not sure why "quit" doesn't quit the function

        elif animal == "quit":
            ...
            return

It does quit the function, by returning. The while loop is abandoned that that point.

        else:
            print("Goodbye!")            
            break

That is another way to quit the function, by halting the loop and falling off the end.

In both cases your function returns None to the caller.

I'm getting an error when a space/nothing is entered

The OP code works fine for me, producing example output such as:

Welcome name. Look at this list of animals:  ['horse', ' ', 'bunny']

parameter

It looks like you want a signature that is closer to this:

def listomatic(name: str = "Matt"):

Then you could execute things like print(f"Welcome {name}.").

side effects

I wouldn't recommend doing things like this:

        print_this3 = print("Enter the name...")

You're evaluating print() for side effects, and then assigning a constant value of None to that temp var. Prefer to just execute the print(), and ignore its return value.

consistent style

Both the return and break techniques in the OP code get the job done. But the needless inconsistency is a bit jarring for a maintenance engineer who is reading the code. Prefer to stick with a single style within that function.

match

Those elifs work nicely enough. But you might want to look into using the match statement for such dispatching.

Q: Using group_by with user defined function A:

I don't know exactly what your expected result is, but perhaps this will help you. As I suggest in my first comment, dplyr's group_xxxx family of functions may well be the way to go. In this case, group_modify may be slightly more efficient than group_map. (group_map will still work, but you'll need to add bind_rows to the pipe to get the same result.)

The group_xxxx family of functions apply a function (defined by group_xxx's argument) to each group of a grouped data frame. If the data frame isn't grouped, the function is applied to the entire data frame.

The user supplied function need to define two arguments, conventionally named .x and .y. .x is the current group of the input data frame. .y is a single row data frame that contains the definition of the current group. I don't think we need to use .y here, but we still need to define it.

So, making minimal changes to your function (though there are others I would make if I were writing it myself...), you could write

library(tidyverse)

progressionby19 <- function(.x, .y) {
  total <- .x %>%  
    filter(Student.Attended == "Yes") %>% 
    summarise(count = n_distinct(Student.ID))
  
  progressed <- .x %>%  
    filter(
      Student.Attended == "Yes",
      entryby19 == "Yes"
    ) %>% 
    summarise(count = n_distinct(Student.ID))
  
  total %>% mutate(progression_rate = (progressed$count/total$count)*100)
}

And then apply the function using group_modify:

example %>% 
  group_by(Type) %>% 
  group_modify(progressionby19)

Giving

# A tibble: 2 × 3
# Groups:   Type [2]
  Type       count progression_rate
  <chr>      <int>            <dbl>
1 Exhibition     2              100
2 Mentoring      2               50

Is that anything close to what you want? If not, you really need to give us more information...

Postscript

The following function gives the same result as the one above but is, in my opinion, easier to understand.

progressionby19 <- function(.x, .y) {
  .x %>%  
    filter(Student.Attended == "Yes") %>% 
    summarise(
      count = n(),
      progression_rate = 100 * mean(entryby19 == "Yes")
    )
}

Q: Prevent duplicates from adding items from Listbox1 to Listbox2 A:

In case anyone is still interested, there's another way to do this, using a similar technique. 

Sub Duplicate()

 dim i as integer
 dim x as integer
 x = 0

  For i = 0 to listbox2.count - 1 
     If listbox2.list(i) = myval Then
        x = x + 1
     End If
  Next i

  If x = 0 Then
     listbox2.additem myval
  End If

End Sub

Where myval is the selected value from listbox1.

Essentially if it finds a single reference to your value in the list, it will start a counter. If no instances of your value are found, it will insert it into the listbox.

Hope this helps someone.
